_note: Avatar SLICES are exclusive per client. A new client cannot claim a slice already in claimed_slices. The niche research pool is shared; the psychographic territory is not.

claimed_slices.demographic: HDB upgraders, 32-38, married, 1-2 kids, Malay-Singaporean, dual income S$8k-14k household
claimed_slices.psychographic: Aspirational but paralysed — wants private property / EC but anxious about timing, CPF refund math, and agent self-interest. Procrastinating 1-2 years. Responds to systematic clarity frameworks over hard sell.
deep_fears_top3: Selling HDB at the wrong time and losing the profit window
Missing the BTO / post-MOP timing and being priced out permanently
Agent pushing them into a purchase for commission, not their benefit
claimed_slices.core_desire: Upgrade without getting screwed — mathematical certainty before committing

available_slices_property_sg: BTO ballot losers — waited 5+ years, now forced into resale / private market unexpectedly
Expat PR holders eyeing landed or good-class bungalow — different income profile, different fear set
Empty nesters downsizing — condo or private to HDB, equity release driven
Investment-grade rental yield buyers — pure numbers decision, yield vs capital appreciation
Divorce-driven forced sellers — emotionally loaded, time-pressured, need non-judgmental advisory
Inheritance property inheritors — unsure whether to sell, rent, or move in
First-time private buyers (no HDB history) — younger, higher income, different CPF considerations
Singles under 35 buying resale HDB — MOP clock starts late, want to know exit strategy early
Pre-retirement downsize planners — 55+ selling large private to unlock CPF OA
Cross-ethnic upgrader couples — mixed financial profiles, navigating HDB ethnic quota
EC buyers riding TOP window — just got keys, deciding on immediate sell vs rent vs hold
claim_rule: A new client CANNOT claim a slice already listed in claimed_slices. They must either: (a) pick from available_slices_property_sg, or (b) propose a NEW slice with a written non-overlap justification validated against existing claimed_slices. Both demographic AND psychographic must be meaningfully distinct — same demographic with a different emotional entry point counts as a new slice if the psychographic is genuinely different.
overlap_check_prompt: Before finalising a new client's avatar, run this check: does the proposed slice share (1) the same demographic band AND (2) the same core fear / core desire as any existing claimed_slices entry? If yes to both, it is not a new slice — redirect the client to an unclaimed segment or split the demographic more narrowly.
reclaim_rule: A slice can be released back to available by setting the client field to null and documenting the release_reason + release_date. Released slices return to the available pool after 90 days (to allow creative assets to age out of market).
